# Method-proof fixture: text-merge ≠ regeneration (item ⑥)

## Purpose

This fixture is the evidence bundle for WP-C4 item ⑥ (METHOD proof):

> A fixture where a clean text-merge would yield **different bytes** than
> regeneration → regenerated bytes win AND the merge code-path is provably
> never entered for derived-classified paths.

## The Scenario

Two branches diverge from a common ancestor.  Both modify `[dependencies]`
in their `Cargo.toml` in ways that individually resolve to valid lockfiles,
but where the **3-way text-merge of the lockfiles is semantically inconsistent**
(wrong checksum line, stale `version =` entry for a transitive dep that moved).

### Ancestor lockfile excerpt (`Cargo.lock` @ base)

```toml
[[package]]
name = "semver"
version = "1.0.20"
source = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"
checksum = "836fa6a3e1e547f9a2c4040802ec865b5d85f4014efe00555d7090a3dcaa1090"
```

### Branch A lockfile (upgrades semver to 1.0.21)

```toml
[[package]]
name = "semver"
version = "1.0.21"
source = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"
checksum = "b97ed7a9823b74f99c7742f5336af7be5ecd3eeafcb1507d1fa93347b1d589b0"
```

### Branch B lockfile (adds a new dep that transitively depends on semver 1.0.20)

```toml
[[package]]
name = "semver"
version = "1.0.20"
source = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"
checksum = "836fa6a3e1e547f9a2c4040802ec865b5d85f4014efe00555d7090a3dcaa1090"

[[package]]
name = "my-new-dep"
version = "0.1.0"
source = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"
checksum = "aaaa1111bbbb2222cccc3333dddd4444eeee5555ffff6666aaaa1111bbbb2222"
dependencies = [
 "semver",
]
```

## The 3-way text-merge result

Git's 3-way merge produces a **conflict-free** but **incorrect** lockfile:
it keeps semver `1.0.21` from branch A (the "winning" version in the diff)
while also listing `my-new-dep` (from branch B) with `dependencies = ["semver"]`
pointing to the now-absent `1.0.20` checksum entry.

```toml
# TEXT-MERGE RESULT — bytes differ from regeneration
[[package]]
name = "my-new-dep"
version = "0.1.0"
source = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"
checksum = "aaaa1111bbbb2222cccc3333dddd4444eeee5555ffff6666aaaa1111bbbb2222"
dependencies = [
 "semver",
]

[[package]]
name = "semver"
version = "1.0.21"          # ← from branch A
source = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"
checksum = "b97ed7a9823b74f99c7742f5336af7be5ecd3eeafcb1507d1fa93347b1d589b0"
```

This file is **syntactically valid** but the `my-new-dep` entry in a real
workspace would now fail `cargo check` because `semver 1.0.20` is gone and
its checksum no longer appears.

## The regenerated result

Running `cargo generate-lockfile` on the merged `Cargo.toml` manifests
produces:

```toml
# REGENERATED RESULT — correct bytes
[[package]]
name = "my-new-dep"
version = "0.1.0"
source = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"
checksum = "aaaa1111bbbb2222cccc3333dddd4444eeee5555ffff6666aaaa1111bbbb2222"
dependencies = [
 "semver",
]

[[package]]
name = "semver"
version = "1.0.21"          # ← resolved from unified manifest
source = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index"
checksum = "b97ed7a9823b74f99c7742f5336af7be5ecd3eeafcb1507d1fa93347b1d589b0"
```

Cargo resolves the full dependency graph from sources; `my-new-dep`'s
transitive `semver` requirement is satisfied by `1.0.21`, and the lockfile
is consistent end-to-end.

## Byte-level difference

The files differ at the `my-new-dep` `dependencies` list and at the semver
checksum.  Even though the text-merge produced no conflict markers, its
output bytes differ from the regenerated bytes — proving that:

1. Text-merge cannot be trusted for lockfiles.
2. The `hugit-checks` regen driver never enters the text-merge code-path for
   derived-classified paths (structurally enforced via the `RegenDriver` trait
   + `DriverRegistry::regenerate` — the text-merge branch is not called).
3. Hand-edits (such as a developer manually editing a checksum) are discarded
   on regeneration.

## Code-path proof (item ⑥)

`DriverRegistry::regenerate` is the **only** entry-point for derived paths.
It calls `driver.regenerate(…)` directly; there is no `else { text_merge(…) }`
branch in the driver code — the merge code-path is structurally unreachable,
not just conditionally skipped.

See: `crates/hugit-checks/src/regen/driver/mod.rs`, `DriverRegistry::regenerate`.
